question:
A thin conducting ring of radius $a$ and total resistance $R$ lies in a horizontal plane. A spatially uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the ring varies with time as
$$B(t)=B_0+\alpha t\quad (\alpha>0).$$
Neglect the ring’s self-inductance so that the induced current at any instant is $I(t)=\dfrac{|\varepsilon(t)|}{R}$. Also neglect mechanical deformation (the ring remains circular).

Find the **instantaneous tension** $T(t)$ in the ring due to the magnetic force on its current-carrying wire at time $t$.
